brief: Controlled header-selector authorization comparison with policy/identity evidence, unchanged authentication, allowed/denied/shared controls and inconclusive treatment of unknowns.
grounding: knowledge_allowed for original methodology; explicit source attribution verified against fetched publisher/maintainer text.

sources.title: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References (WSTG-ATHZ-04)
sources.selection_reason: OWASP maintainer guidance supports object-reference variation using multiple users, known object ownership and application business rules to distinguish unauthorized access.
sources.limits: Does not prescribe the exact header-selector procedure or invalid-value fallback behavior. Identity, control design and interpretation remain original methodology; no live target claim is verified.

sources.title: Testing for Bypassing Authorization Schema (WSTG-ATHZ-02)
sources.selection_reason: OWASP maintainer guidance discusses horizontal/vertical authorization comparisons with distinct sessions, and special request headers that can influence URL selection.
sources.limits: The header examples concern URL overrides rather than all account-selection headers. A changed or unchanged invalid-value response does not establish permission or prove absence of a selector. This technique must retain policy and object evidence.

sources.title: Insecure direct object references (IDOR) — Web Security Academy
sources.selection_reason: The publisher explains user-supplied object selection and a conditional account-record access-control failure when other controls are absent. Supports the draft attribution and the distinction between selection and an authorization failure.
sources.limits: Does not establish any target entitlement, header handling or exploitability. It is conceptual background, not proof of every procedure step.

rejected_fetches.reason: Redirected to generic latest foreword, not the requested test documents; not selected as mechanism evidence.

assessment: Three actually fetched references are useful background. No source independently specifies the complete proposed workflow or proves live target behavior.
